structured.approach: I read both contracted inputs (feat.tasks, org.engineering_stack). The step hook blocks shell commands in DE-01, so I checked ap_pipeline by reading its git metadata (.git/HEAD, .git/config, the HEAD, dev and feature/story reflogs) and its repository files with Read. The files were __init__.py, transform.py, ingest.py, dq.py, pipeline.py, schedule.json, ci.py, README.md, CLAUDE.md and tests/test_pipeline.py. I matched them against the tool view and the TSK-01 and TSK-02 budgets in feat.tasks. Every file cited in the output was read in this session. I used no connectors because the inputs and checkout held the needed facts.

claims.text: Databricks access is not applicable: no repository uses Databricks or a database, and ap_pipeline uses no Databricks or other workspace.
ap_pipeline is available locally, cloned from https://github.com/arghya05/ap-pipeline-sample.git, with branches main and dev tracking origin, so no repository creation is needed.
Branch feature/story is checked out at 3fcbe1b, created from dev, and the agent identity has write access with a clean working tree.
ap_pipeline is at version 0.4.0, matching feat.tasks, which assigns the ap_pipeline version step to TSK-01.
CI is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py with COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0 and static checks for print, eval, exec, bare except and lines longer than 140 characters.

to_model returns (records, rejected) from a single try block, uses the exception class name as the rejection reason, and does not yet handle paid_date; TSK-01 must keep this signature and return shape.
tests/test_pipeline.py exists with test_run_maps_and_rejects, test_paid_flag and test_missing_column_rejected, and is the test file assigned to TSK-01.
The must-not-change files ingest.py, dq.py, pipeline.py and schedule.json (daily, 02:00, Asia/Kolkata) are present.
Feature branches are expected per story, but a single branch named feature/story serves both STORY-01 and STORY-02.
ci.py imports the third-party coverage package although the repository is described as Python 3.9 standard library.

open_questions: RAQ-1 (non-blocking): one branch per story (feature/<story>) is expected, but the single branch feature/story serves STORY-01 and STORY-02. Keep it or split it? Owner: Data engineering lead / spine operator.

RAQ-2 (non-blocking): ci.py imports coverage, which is not in the standard library. DE-01 allows no shell commands, so installation for /usr/bin/python3 is unconfirmed. Confirm at the first CI run. Owner: Data engineering lead.
RAQ-3 (non-blocking): feature/story has no upstream in .git/config. Confirm that the spine sets it when it pushes in DE-10. Owner: Spine operator.
structured.summary: DE-01 passes. ap_pipeline is available locally on feature/story at 3fcbe1b, created from dev, and the agent has write access with a clean tree. No repository needs creating. Databricks is not applicable because no repository uses Databricks or a database. The baseline matches feat.tasks: version 0.4.0, CI with a 90.0 coverage gate, the to_model signature and return shape, and the TSK-01 test file and must-not-change files. Three non-blocking questions remain: the branch-per-story naming, whether coverage is installed, and the upstream for the push.
